attributes.body_ja:
「たとえ」は、「ても」や「でも」と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われる副詞（ふくし）です。ある状況（じょうきょう）を仮定（かてい）して、その状況（じょうきょう）ではふつう予想（よそう）される結果（けっか）とは違（ちが）ったり、あまりよくない結果（けっか）になったりするときによく使（つか）われます。たいてい、文（ぶん）の始（はじ）まりに置（お）かれ、そのあとに仮定（かてい）の内容（ないよう）が続（つづ）きます。

「たとえ」は、「仮（かり）に (A) でも、(B) は変（か）わらない」のように、(A) と (B) は反対（はんたい）の内容（ないよう）になるような場合（ばあい）によく使（つか）われます。それに対（たい）して「もし」は「仮（かり）に (A) なら、(B) になる」のような、(A) が (B) という結果（けっか）につながる使（つか）い方（かた）が多（おお）いです。
attributes.body:
たとえ, coming from 仮令（たとえ）, an adverb meaning 'supposing that', is a word in Japanese that is often used with ても (or でも), in order to present possible circumstances, and their contradictory and/or (usually) undesirable outcomes. たとえ is primarily seen at the beginning of a sentence, before some kind of possibility, comparison, or supposition will be stated.

たとえ tends to be used to present situations where 'even if (A) were true, (B) still may/may not happen'. This is called a 'contrastive' example. もし on the other hand tends to be used for examples in which (A) will directly result in (B). This is called a 'resultative' example.

attributes.description: Revisit ても and check out the examples under 4 and 6

attributes.body: たとえ～ても is a stronger and more limited version of ても used in hypothetical situations. For example, たとえどこに行っても 'no matter where you might go' is a more emphatic version of どこに行っても 'wherever you go'. However, in cases where ても expresses permission, e.g. てもいい 'you can (A)', たとえ would not be used, since the meaning is not strongly hypothetical.

first_relatable.title: たとえ〜ても
first_relatable.meaning: Even if…is the case, Supposing that

attributes.body: もし and たとえ are similar in that both can be used at the beginning of a sentence to emphasize a hypothetical situation or condition. The primary difference is that while もし can be followed by a wide variety of conditionals, including なら, たら, ば, and ても, たとえ is almost always followed by a ても expression, giving it the meaning of 'even if (A)' or 'even supposing that (A)'.

second_relatable.title: たとえ〜ても
second_relatable.meaning: Even if…is the case, Supposing that

attributes.body: にしても and たとえ〜ても both mean 'even if', but にしても leans toward conditions that are reasonably likely, e.g. 難しいにしてもやってみたほうがいい ('Even if it's difficult, you should give it a try'). たとえ〜ても is far more hypothetical, e.g. たとえ失敗してもあきらめない ('Even if I fail, I won't give up').

first_relatable.title: にしても
first_relatable.meaning: Even though, Even if, Even when, Also

second_relatable.title: たとえ〜ても
second_relatable.meaning: Even if…is the case, Supposing that

attributes.body: Both express strong contrary hypotheticals, similar to 'Even if (A), still (B)'. たとえ〜ても is less formal and more common in speech, e.g. たとえ一人でも、ちゃんとやる 'Even if it's just me, I'll do it right.' とも is more literary and formal, and takes the volitional form, e.g. 死のうとも構わない 'Even if I die, I don't mind.'

first_relatable.title: たとえ〜ても
first_relatable.meaning: Even if…is the case, Supposing that

attributes.body: Both express contrastive conditionals. たとえ〜ても is neutral or formal, e.g. たとえ雨に降られても気にしない 'Even if I get rained on, I won't care.' たって is casual and conversational, often used with emotional insistence, e.g. そんなこと言ったってしょうがないよ 'Even if you say that, there's nothing we can do.'

first_relatable.title: たとえ〜ても
first_relatable.meaning: Even if…is the case, Supposing that

second_relatable.title: たって
second_relatable.meaning: Even if, Even though, No matter how

attributes.body: Both express hypothetical conditions, but with different implications. たとえ〜ても presents contrast, like 'Even if (A), still (B)', e.g. たとえ雨が降っても行きます 'Even if it rains, I'll go.' としても assumes (A) as a premise for argument or stance, e.g. 行くとしても一人では行かない 'Even if I go, I won't go alone.'

first_relatable.title: たとえ〜ても
first_relatable.meaning: Even if…is the case, Supposing that

second_relatable.title: としても
second_relatable.meaning: Even if (we assume), Assuming,  Also as

attributes.body: Both introduce hypothetical situations, but with different nuances. たとえ〜ても sets up contrast, like 'Even if (A), still (B)', e.g. たとえ負けても悔いはない 'Even if I lose, I'll have no regrets.' もしも～なら・～でも expresses a basic hypothetical and its result, e.g. もしも彼が来たら、話します 'If he comes, I'll talk to him.'

attributes.body: Both show that something remains unchanged regardless of conditions. たとえ〜ても presents a contrasting hypothetical, e.g. たとえ雨に降られても気にしない 'Even if I get rained on, I won't care.' にせよ・にしろ is more concrete and neutral, often listing options, e.g. 行くにせよ行かないにせよ、連絡してほしい 'Whether you go or not, I want you to contact me.'
